text:
Elias Lindholm's time in Boston had been underwhelming, and last season Evolving-Hockey had him at replacement level (-0.4 wins). This season he looks like the two-way center the Bruins paid for. He has 6 goals and 14 points in 17 games, Boston is winning his minutes at 5v5 (54.6 percent of expected goals with him on), and he finished off the Blackhawks with an overtime winner on Oct. 31. The Boston Herald's read is that a healthy Lindholm is a different player, and the ice time agrees: he is up near 18 minutes a night over his last ten.

Now the caution. His team has scored 5.5 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and he is shooting 20.7 percent. Both of those come down. The underlying piece worth keeping is his passing: Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has 23 percent of his setups going across the royal road, more than triple a typical forward. Expect the points to slow; the play itself looks real.
headline: Lindholm looks like himself, with help from the bounces
